sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Washington County, Florida?
sections.html:
The Washington County Tax Collector bills and collects, and the county property appraiser sets each parcel's value. The collector's office is in Chipley, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with a separate post office box for mail.

The collector's millage page spells out who sets what. The Board of County Commissioners sets the county rate, the School Board sets the school rates, each city council sets the rate for its municipality, and special districts set their own. The same page says the property appraiser establishes the value of real estate and tangible personal property.

That division is useful to a seller. A question about the value or an exemption belongs with the appraiser, and a question about the amount owed or a certificate belongs with the collector.

sections.h2: Which taxing bodies appear on a Washington County bill?
sections.html:
The collector's millage page lists seven levies for 2026: Chipley, Vernon, the county, Northwest Florida Water Management, and three school levies. The rates are printed as decimals, so a figure like .00850000 means 8.5 mills. Confirm which are final with the tax collector before you rely on them, since the page does not say the rates are adopted.

sections.h2: What are the Washington County tax deadlines?
sections.html:
Collection starts in November and runs through March 31, with a falling discount. The tax collector's deadline page sets out the year.

  • November: collection begins, with a 4% discount for payment by November 30.
  • December: 3% discount.
  • January: 2% discount. February: 1% discount.
  • March 31: gross amount due, and the final installment payment is due.
  • April 1: unpaid real property tax is delinquent and a 3% penalty is added.
  • April 30: applications for next year's installment plan are due.

The page says delinquent real property is advertised within 45 days of the delinquency and that the cost is added to the bill. The list is advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the certificate sale. It also says the sale date is set in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency.

sections.h2: How does the Washington County installment plan run?
sections.html:
The plan is built on four payments through the year. The deadlines page puts the first due on or before June 1, with cancellation if it is not paid by June 30, the second before September 30, the third by December 31, and the fourth by March 31. Taxpayers already enrolled do not reapply.

The application window closes April 30 for the next year. Escrowed owners usually have no use for it, since the lender pays in full.

Statewide, an owner may apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year under s. 197.222, per the Department of Revenue. Ask the office which form and which amount applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What does a tax certificate mean for a Washington County house?
sections.html:
A certificate is a lien created when someone pays your delinquent tax. It is not a purchase of the property. The collector holds the sale on or before June 1 for the prior year's unpaid taxes.

The page describes how the amount is built: unpaid real estate tax and non ad valorem assessments, a 3% penalty, a 5% collector commission and advertising costs. Bidding opens at 18% and goes down, and the winning rate is what the owner pays. If the interest earned is under 5%, a 5% minimum applies.

  • A homestead parcel whose face value is under $250 is not sold to the public. The certificate goes to the county at 18%.
  • Certificates are dated as of the first day of the sale and expire after seven years.
  • Redemption requires certified funds in US dollars.

The office warns that failing to redeem within the 22 month period set by law can result in loss of the property at a tax deed sale. The state counts two years from April 1 of the issue year before a holder can apply, per s. 197.502. The collector also runs an online tax sale site, taxcertsale.com/WashingtonTaxSale.

sections.h2: How do exemptions change what a Washington County buyer pays?
sections.html:
Exemptions stay with the owner and do not pass to a buyer. The appraiser's deadline is March 1, and the owner must have made the home a permanent residence by January 1, per the Department of Revenue's homestead guide.

The state's Save Our Homes cap ties yearly assessment growth to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and a sale resets the property to just value the following January 1, per the Department of Revenue. A buyer should not assume the seller's lower bill carries over.

A seller's final bill therefore tells the buyer very little about next year's bill. Ask the property appraiser for the value and exemptions on the parcel.

sections.h2: What should a Washington County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Call the collector in Chipley and ask for the amount good through the planned closing date. Then give it to the title agent. The collector's page notes that the 3% penalty arrives April 1 and the advertising cost shortly after, so selling before that date is cheaper.

At recording, the clerk collects deed stamps. The Department of Revenue says the rate is 70 cents per $100 for all counties except Miami-Dade, and that every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay, per its stamp tax page.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. The Washington County Tax Collector's page says a 3% penalty is added to the gross amount on that date.

faqs.q: What is the first discount month in Washington County?
faqs.a: November, with a 4% discount on payments made by November 30. December is 3%, January 2% and February 1%.

faqs.q: Can a homestead owner lose a house over a small debt?
faqs.a: Not to a public sale of the certificate for a small amount. The collector says a homestead parcel with a face value under $250 is issued to the county at 18% interest instead of being sold.

faqs.q: How long does a certificate stay valid in Washington County?
faqs.a: Seven years. Certificates are dated from the first day of the sale and then expire.

faqs.q: Where do I find current Washington County millage rates?
faqs.a: On the tax collector's millage rates page, which lists the 2026 levies for the county, Chipley, Vernon, the school board and the water management district. Ask the office to confirm which rates are final.
